item.text: {"question_id":"5B.4","answer":"The evidence shows some ruler-attributed creation of competition and investment rules, but not consistently fair or predictable implementation across the economy. The Bundestag passed the 11th Competition Act amendment in July 2023, strengthening sector investigations, benefit-skimming, merger powers, and possible structural remedies; the Federal Cartel Office also reported ongoing enforcement, including merger conditions, digital-platform cases, energy-price-brake reviews, and a functioning competition register. However, the source describes new powers and institutional activity more than completed market outcomes, and does not establish Scholz’s personal authorship or intervention (BATCH-0007-E007). Labor, minimum-wage, working-time, and occupational-safety rules were reported as effectively enforced, but the quantitative inspection evidence is mainly from 2022, and the same report records employer interference with works-council organization and exclusions or limitations affecting some workers (BATCH-0009-E020). Other rules were materially less predictable: the Supply Chain Act had limited reach, constrained administrative enforcement, and no general court liability (BATCH-0008-E009); smart-meter legislation was enacted but experts identified unresolved cost, capacity, privacy, social-distribution, and implementation problems, while the 2030 rollout remained an objective rather than an observed outcome (BATCH-0009-E002; BATCH-0009-E003); and heat-planning proposals drew warnings about bureaucracy, staffing, financing, coordination, and unrealistic or insufficient targets, without proof here of eventual implementation failure (BATCH-0009-E009). Digital-administration targets were missed, with only 105 of 575 services online at the end-2022 target date, and experts judged the 2023 amendment insufficient on standards, timelines, costs, monitoring, and technical coordination; this shortfall began before Scholz and is not solely attributable to him (BATCH-0009-E012). The DSA implementation deadline was also missed by several months, creating uncertainty for smaller providers and delaying trusted-flagger registration, though some criticism postdated 2023 (BATCH-0010-E004). Housing approvals fell 26.6% in 2023, with declines across private, company, public, single-family, two-family, and multifamily applications, but Destatis attributed the result partly to material costs and financing conditions and did not identify a federal policy cause (BATCH-0023-E001; BATCH-0023-E002; BATCH-0023-E003). Scholz’s own account reports laws prioritizing renewable-energy and grid expansion and faster approvals, but it is an official representation not independently verified here (BATCH-0032-E004). Overall, the record supports formal rulemaking and some enforcement, alongside substantial implementation, predictability, coverage, and outcome gaps; responsibility is shared among the federal government, Bundestag, Länder, regulators, municipalities, courts, and market conditions.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0007-E007","BATCH-0009-E020","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0032-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E009","BATCH-0009-E002","BATCH-0009-E009","BATCH-0009-E012","BATCH-0010-E004","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0023-E002","BATCH-0023-E003","BATCH-0003-E009"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence provides limited direct measurement of competition, firm entry, entrepreneurship, property-rights security, trade, investment, job creation, or business-level incidence.","Several favorable enforcement claims rely on institutional activity, planned powers, or 2022 data rather than 2023 outcomes.","Housing, digital, energy, and administrative outcomes have substantial non-federal, inherited, technical, financing, and market-related causes.","No supplied evidence establishes comprehensive, consistently fair enforcement across sectors or directly attributes all implementation failures to Scholz personally."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported characterization of maintained meaningful enforcement capacity as a general 2023 finding.","Separated enacted laws, institutional enforcement activity, expert warnings, implementation shortfalls, and outcomes.","Reduced the weight given to skilled-immigration and supply-chain measures because the evidence shows staged implementation, limited reach, or no demonstrated effects.","Added the omitted digital-administration shortfall and DSA implementation delay with their attribution limits.","Qualified housing evidence as an outcome with multiple causes rather than evidence of a government-specific regulatory failure."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
